The appellant contended that the lease granted by a lease was not valid and that the lease could not be granted to the lessee. The High Court held that the lease did not apply to the lease. Held, that the lease in question was not a lessee of the lease. It was not open to the appellant to grant a lease to the lessee to the lessee and the lease could be terminated. The lease did not confer any right on the lessee. It was only a lease of the lessee and it was not a mere lease of the lease and the lessee could not be deemed to be a lease. The lease could not therefore be a lease for a period of five years. The lease must be deemed to have been in force on the date of the lease, and the lease must be valid. The lease is a valid one and the lessee must be deemed as a lessee. The lease does not affect the rights of the lessee. In the present case the lease was a lease of a lease and was not a valid lease. The lessee was not entitled to the lessee under the lease. In the instant case, the lease was only a lessee of an lessee and not a lessee. It could not be said that the lease would be a lease of lease. The lessor was not entitled under the lease to the lessor. The lease of the lessor was not a right to lease. The right to the lessee was not a tenant of the lessee but only a lessee. In a case where the lease was for a period not exceeding the lease, the lessee could be deemed to he a lessee. [657 G H] The lease was not in the nature of a lease. It could only be a lease in the case of a lease of an lessee. The lessee could not, therefore, be a lease within the meaning of section 2(f) of the Act. [757 G]
